title: Visibility Is Not Detection: Auditing Measurement Boundaries in Staged and Evidence-Ranking Evaluation
title_note: Current title adopted by the 2026-10-21 canonical integration. The 2026-10-11 title and earlier working variants remain historical records and are not active submission wording.
thesis: A bounded two-case measurement audit separates visibility, detection, harmfulness, score sensitivity, decision stability and reproduction gap: Case 1 audits a staged document evaluator with FinQA as a nested boundary probe, and Case 2 audits FinRank with preregistered v1 tie metrics and thresholds plus a post-hoc v2 identity correction. The six-step review sequence is a proposed checklist, not a validated universal method.

claims.claim: Visibility, detection and harmfulness are distinct constructs and the frozen evaluator has family-specific observation boundaries. The OCR-like 0/13 boundary is a non-response on the frozen scored surface; it is not by itself evidence of harmful detection failure, and an existing single judge classified all 13 cases as referentially equivalent under its table-context contract.

In the single-responsive-leaf construction the unrounded flat and hierarchical scores are a positive affine/rank transform of one another and retain identical ranks, so corresponding decisions are structurally equivalent; separately, the zero-by-construction clean panel leaves the registered deployment operating point unresolved, which is a calibration degeneracy and not a general non-identifiability of matched-FPR comparisons. In the controlled multi-leaf construction, stage-aligned instrumentation carries the separable signature, the direct three-leaf codebook matches the full vector, and the non-direct leaves carry partial stage information (they separate mapping from retrieval/numeric but not retrieval from numeric) rather than none.

As a nested boundary probe inside Case 1, the frozen FinQA v2 result (formal class SECOND_FLOW_MIXED) is consistent with a measurement-object mismatch: the detection predicate is defined and the V/D/O counts are reproducible, but the downstream result fields it consumes are not regenerated from the perturbed program, so the counts do not estimate detection ability. Cross-dataflow causal alignment is a design requirement, not a validated law. FinQA is not a third Paper E case and is not evidence of protocol blindness (both terms are defined in `definitions`).

The FinRank v1 tie metrics and materiality thresholds are preregistered and unchanged. Under ties-positive, strict-win and half-credit pairwise scoring, absolute random-negative accuracy is score-sensitive, while the qualitative hard-versus-random decision is stable under the tested tie alternatives: TF-IDF gap 14.179/13.821/14.000 and BM25 gap 13.009/12.666/12.838 percentage points for ties-positive/strict/half-credit. Displayed values are independently rounded from full precision. Score sensitivity and decision stability are separate constructs.

The canonical trimmed/`text_sha1` identity counts are post-hoc v2 corrections after the wrong-identity v1 application: 442 cross-record overlapping hard negatives across 305 records, with first-occurrence metadata gold loss in 33 records and all-gold loss in 2. V1's raw-exact 293/220 result is preserved as superseded wrong-identity evidence. Residual global and metadata metric drift is exposed (up to 0.19 and 0.16 points in the declared deterministic environment), while in-record and pairwise metrics reproduce exactly; the drift cause remains unresolved.

definitions.protocol blindness: An evaluation protocol that cannot observe a defect under any tested observation surface or threshold within its frozen configuration. Used only as a defined alternative; the paper does not claim or exclude it without this definition.
definitions.MEASUREMENT_OBJECT_MISMATCH: The perturbation and the detection rule operate on different measurement objects, so the detection predicate cannot respond to the perturbation by construction; this is a statement about object alignment, not about detector quality.
definitions.SECOND_FLOW_MIXED: The frozen formal result class of the FinQA v2 second-dataflow run: a mixed observation/detection pattern produced under a construction that was not causally aligned. A classification only; it is not a performance or transfer claim.
definitions.M aliasing (Route B): Two M-stage leaf slots written from the same predicate, so the source-local / downstream partition is not separable (MVP design audit, filed HIGH).
definitions.R/N downstream non-estimability (Route B: For stages R and N no downstream checkpoint responded on the frozen carriers, so the downstream causal term could not be estimated.
definitions.harmfulness equivalence-dependence: Harmfulness is defined relative to a stated equivalence contract; changing the contract can change the label (hence the boundary framing).
definitions.score sensitivity: The movement of an absolute metric under a changed score or tie contract; it does not by itself imply a changed benchmark decision.
definitions.decision stability: Preservation of the qualitative decision or ordering supported by the benchmark under tested contract alternatives; it does not imply exact score reproduction.
definitions.reproduction gap: A mismatch between independently executed and released metric values under a stated environment and tolerance; its cause is not assigned without sufficient evidence.
